# Working Capital Analysis

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. Working capital moves are operational, not free money: stretching payables can damage supplier relationships, tightening collections can cost customers, the cash a day of cycle is worth can be lost again to growth, and no release estimate here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the working capital analysis skill of GAJETOso/financeskills, written from the seat of a working capital manager. Use it when cash feels tied up, or on DSO, DPO, DIO, cash conversion cycle, AR aging, payment terms or working capital peg questions, including in a deal context. The data set comes first: monthly balances for receivables, inventory, payables and other working capital items over at least 24 months, with the honest warning that month-ends hide intra-month peaks, plus revenue and COGS by month, agings, and the top customer and supplier terms, all read against seasonality, growth (which consumes working capital mechanically) and any covenant pressure. The core metrics are computed in code: DSO, DIO and DPO in days, the cash conversion cycle as their sum and difference, and the cash value of one day of cycle, with countback DSO for seasonal businesses because the simple version lies when sales swing. Every deterioration is decomposed into volume, terms and discipline: a rising DSO is traced to mix shift, terms creep, billing delays, disputes or collection slack through the aging waterfall...
